title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: 52% plan to give to fewer people or buy fewer holiday gifts this year
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**ALL I WANT FOR CHRISTMAS**


Holiday gift recipients increasingly prefer an experience over a traditional gift, based on[The Holiday Edit](https://theharrispoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2026-Holiday-Thought-Leadership-FULL-REPORT-3.pdf) report from Harris Poll.


- The most preferred holiday gifts this season are experiences to be enjoyed together (19%), a gift card for a store or restaurant (17%), cash to use however the recipient wants (17%), experiences to enjoy alone (7%) and donation to a cause (4%).
- 59% expect to enter the season under some form of financial constraint.
- 52% plan to give to fewer people or buy fewer gifts per person.
- 45% rank meaningful time with loved ones among their top three ingredients for a successful holiday.
- As budgets tighten, two-thirds will protect gatherings and shared meals, and 56% will cut gifts or treats for themselves first.
- 59% plan to use rewards or loyalty points to lower spending, and nearly half (47%) will shorten trips, stay closer to home or choose cheaper travel.
- 54% wish their gift-exchange partners would agree to stop buying gifts for one another.
- *See also:[Gen Z and Millennials will let AI pick the gifts, but they still want the final say](https://www.mastercard.com/us/en/news-and-trends/stories/2026/ai-holiday-gift-giving-gen-z-millennials.html)*


**A WORLD OF WORRY**


People are struggling to envision a better tomorrow, yet they are looking for ways to spark hope, according to the[Vision Void](https://theharrispoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Business-of-Creativity-deck-November-2026-The-Harris-Poll.pdf) research from Harris Poll.


- 70% feel the world is changing faster than they can keep up with.
- 65% say they are “grieving a version of the world that no longer exists.”
- 84% in the UK and 66% in the U.S. think future geopolitical instability will become worse.
- Most people (89% in the UK and 82% in the U.S.) feel their country is suffering an affordability crisis.
- A majority of Gen Z – 80% in the U.S. and 74% in the UK – feel lonely on the weekends.
- Many (65% in the U.S. and 77% in the UK) rely on their phone for their social life.
- *See also* :[32% of British consumers say information from brands is less trustworthy than five years ago](https://lnkd.in/p/gEfQicDU)


**SCIENCE HAS A TRUST PROBLEM**


Misinformation, political interference and funding worries threaten America’s next health and science breakthroughs, according to new research from The Harris Poll and[Bayer](https://theharrispoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Harris-Poll_Warning-Signs-Report_November-2026.pdf) .


- 89% of doctors, 91% of scientists and 95% of graduate students are concerned about science and health misinformation spreading online.
- 9 in 10 doctors say false or misleading science and health information can lead people to make decisions that negatively affect their health.
- 81% of doctors and 84% of scientists believe the U.S. risks losing talented science and health professionals to other countries.
- With enough R&D funding and investment, 91% of doctors believe we’re only a few years away from solving some of humanity’s most urgent health challenges.
- *See also:[Allison’s Jaime Dowd named to PRWeek Health Influencer 30 list](https://www.prweek.com/article/1974588/2026-health-influencer-30-jamie-dowd)*


**SUCESSION READINESS IS MAJOR BUSINESS ISSUE**


With major CEO successions in the news, a leadership-readiness gap exists as outdated succession practices collide with rising turnover and unclear career paths, based on The State of Succession Planning from Harris Poll and[Wharton Executive Education](https://news.wharton.upenn.edu/press-releases/2026/11/wharton-executive-education-releases-global-research-on-succession-planning/) .


- 86% say succession planning is critical to organizational success.
- 48% believe their organization is very prepared for a leadership transition.
- 67% say their organization’s succession planning approach hasn’t changed in a decade.
- 47% report higher senior executive turnover than five years ago, while 69% say their organization underestimates the risk of senior-level departures.
- 69% say executive advancement paths are not clearly defined, and 70% report a lack of transparency in how new leaders are selected.
- 45% have left a company because advancement paths were unclear.
